plan.intent: Change the customer-facing money precision in src/format/money.js from whole pounds (PLACES = 0) to whole pence (PLACES = 2), so roundMoney/formatMoney — and orderTotal, which still ends in a single roundMoney call — never emit long decimals; the production change stays confined to that one module, as no other file formats money. The canonical advance from 15f926b to 02c749c is unrelated to this plan: it only made account search match on email as well as name, touching src/search/accounts.js (searchAccounts, accounts, needle) and test/search.test.js. Neither file is claimed by this plan, no config key, dependency, API or schema changed, and no money formatting or rounding path was affected, so every file assumption from the previous plan still holds and nothing is stale. Carried forward from the earlier surcharge commit: src/pricing/total.js applies cardSurcharge inside the existing single roundMoney call, so no rounding was added, moved, or duplicated and src/pricing/surcharge.js needs no edit. What still must change alongside the constant is the test expectations — test/total.test.js asserts whole-pound integers for cases that are fractional in pence (card order 57 for a true 56.70, 131 for 131.04, 129 for 128.52, and the discounted free-delivery cases), and test/surcharge.test.js may likewise state assertions at pound precision since the five-percent surcharge is the main source of sub-penny amounts; both must be restated to two decimals. test/export.test.js, test/webhook.test.js and test/search.test.js remain excluded — their assertions concern column layout, retry counts and search matching, not money precision — and the full `node --test` run still covers them and will catch incidental fallout. No edits are needed in src/pricing/total.js, src/pricing/surcharge.js, src/pricing/tax.js, src/pricing/discount.js, src/export/csv.js, src/notify/webhook.js or src/search/accounts.js.

plan.intent: Add a new pricing rule: a 5% card surcharge applied in orderTotal on top of the full otherwise-payable amount (line items less discount, plus delivery, plus handling, plus tax). The surcharge logic lives in a new src/pricing/surcharge.js (CARD_RATE, cardSurcharge) with its own test/surcharge.test.js, matching the repository's one-module-one-test convention (note the new charge in README.md if it documents pricing rules). Only card-paid orders change; any other or unspecified payment method keeps its current total, so every existing total assertion passes unchanged. Placement in src/pricing/total.js is unchanged from the previous plan: orderTotal computes lines -> discounted -> withCharges = discounted + deliveryFor(discounted) + HANDLING -> roundMoney(withCharges + taxFor(withCharges, order)), and the surcharge goes on the post-tax subtotal immediately before the single roundMoney call — roundMoney(subtotal + cardSurcharge(subtotal, order)) — so it stacks on delivery, handling and tax. Critically, the surcharge must NOT be folded into the value passed to deliveryFor: free delivery is judged on the discounted basket only (test/total.test.js asserts this via "free delivery is judged on the discounted basket"), and letting the card uplift move an order across the 100 threshold would break that rule and its tests. DELIVERY, HANDLING, deliveryFor and FREE_DELIVERY_FROM are read-only context for placing the surcharge, not things to change. Since this plan was last written, src/pricing/tax.js changed: taxFor now returns 0 for digital-only orders (new isDigitalOnly helper over order lines; STANDARD_RATE otherwise). This does not move the surcharge — total.js still calls taxFor(withCharges, order) exactly as before, and the surcharge simply applies to whatever post-tax subtotal results, so a digital-only card order is surcharged on an untaxed subtotal. Do not modify src/pricing/tax.js or test/tax.test.js; its four assertions must keep passing. Two other prior changes also remain outside this work and must not be touched: src/pricing/discount.js loyalty tiering (consumed only through the existing discountRate call) and src/audit/log.js IP recording. New total.test.js cases should compare a card order against the same order without a payment method, at both a below-threshold and an at-or-above-threshold basket, to pin that the surcharge is applied after free delivery is decided.
